sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File header and imports
sections.what: States the file's purpose and brings in the typing and Pydantic tools used to define the recipe shapes.
sections.why: Likely reason: the header states the portability rule so readers know recipes stay free of evidence claims.

sections.name: AssemblyVector
sections.title: Three-part position or size
sections.what: Describes a point or measurement with three numbers, each limited to plus or minus one million. Infinite and not-a-number values are rejected.
sections.why: Likely reason: the limit keeps values within a range the viewer and exporters can handle.
sections.watch_out: Other model code describes sizes in metres, so values here should be read the same way.

sections.name: AssemblyDimensions
sections.title: Positive size
sections.what: Describes a size with three numbers, each above zero and at most one hundred thousand.
sections.why: Likely reason: a part with zero or negative size cannot be drawn.
sections.watch_out: Zero is rejected, so a flat part must still have a small positive thickness.

sections.name: AssemblyGeometry
sections.title: Geometry of one recipe part
sections.what: Describes one shape: its type, which is box or cylinder, its size, position, and rotation. A cylinder must have equal X and Z sizes.
sections.why: Likely reason: a cylinder's round cross section is set by its X and Z sizes, so they must match.
sections.watch_out: A cylinder's length is in the Y size, so mixing up the axes produces a wrong shape.

sections.name: AssemblyPartRecipe
sections.title: One part recipe
sections.what: Describes one kind of part: its slot name, role, geometry, material key, how many copies to make, and the offset between copies. The slot name cannot start with a number sign or contain one.
sections.why: Likely reason: the number sign is reserved for numbering copies, so slot names must avoid it.
sections.watch_out: A slot name containing a number sign is rejected, which protects the numbering scheme.

sections.name: AssemblyDefinition
sections.title: Full assembly definition
sections.what: Describes a list of one to 256 recipes. Slot names must be unique, and the total number of expanded parts can be at most 4096.
sections.why: Likely reason: the limit of 4096 keeps one assembly small enough to expand and draw.
sections.watch_out: The 4096 limit is separate from the 100,000-part limit for the whole model, so both must be respected.

sections.name: AssemblyTemplate
sections.title: Named template
sections.what: Adds a template ID and a name of up to 80 characters to the definition. The name cannot be blank.
sections.why: Likely reason: a name lets people find and pick a saved arrangement.
sections.watch_out: A blank name is rejected, but spaces inside a name are kept.

summary: Defines the shape and limits of an assembly recipe: its shape types, sizes, positions, repeats, and template names.
purpose: Sets the rules that a saved or sent recipe must follow, so the app rejects bad recipes before expanding them.
why: The file header says recipes contain no asset identity or transferable evidence claims. Likely reason: recipes are meant to be portable, so they carry only geometry and naming.
how: Uses Pydantic models that forbid unknown fields and check each value. Recipes are grouped into a definition, which is grouped into a named template.
inputs: Recipe values from a user or from a saved template.
outputs: Validated recipe objects, or validation errors naming the broken rule.
risks: Changing a range or a limit affects every saved template and every recipe that depends on it. The recipe limits are separate from the model-wide part budget.
debug: Read the validation error, which names the field and the rule broken. Check slot names for the number sign, which is not allowed, and repeat counts between one and 256.
